integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.subtitle: Monitoring opens and resolves incidents by itself, webhooks pass ticket events to external systems

monitoring.intro: Each source gets its own token. Repeated alerts do not create new tickets, higher severity raises impact and urgency, and a recovery resolves the incident.
monitoring.emptyHint: Connect Zabbix, Alertmanager or Grafana and incidents will appear in the queue by themselves
monitoring.name: Name
monitoring.requesterHint: Leave empty to create a service user “Monitoring: name”
monitoring.minSeverityHint: Less important events are only logged
monitoring.mapping: Impact and urgency by alert severity
monitoring.mappingHint: Incident priority comes from the priority matrix
monitoring.autoResolve: Resolve the incident when the problem is gone
monitoring.autoResolveHint: If nobody has taken the incident yet, a note is added instead

token.title: Token for “{{name}}”
token.once: Copy the token now: after closing this window it cannot be shown again, only reissued.

setup.title: How to connect
setup.zabbixSteps: In Zabbix: Alerts → Media types → Create, type “Webhook”. Add the parameters from the table, paste the script below and assign the media type to a user in a trigger action (including recovery).
setup.zabbixMacros: Define global macros {$EASYITSM.URL} (endpoint), {$EASYITSM.TOKEN} (token) and {$ZABBIX.URL} (Zabbix frontend URL).
setup.alertmanagerSteps: Prometheus Alertmanager: add a receiver to alertmanager.yml. send_resolved is required for auto-resolve.
setup.grafanaSteps: Grafana Alerting: a Webhook contact point with a Bearer authorization header.
setup.genericSteps: Any system that can send an HTTP request: fingerprint groups events of one problem, status is firing or resolved.

webhooks.intro: A webhook sends an event to an external system when an automation rule with the “Send webhook” action fires. Requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 and retried up to 9 times with growing delays.
webhooks.allowedHint: Host name, *.domain or CIDR network. Internal networks only by exact host or network; the server itself and cloud metadata are always denied.
webhooks.allowedEmpty: The list is empty: webhooks are not sent anywhere. Add receiver hosts.
webhooks.urlHint: https:// or http://. The host must be in the allowed addresses.
webhooks.secretOnce: The key is shown once. Store it in the receiving system: later it can only be rotated.
webhooks.verify: The receiver checks X-EasyITSM-Signature: HMAC-SHA256 of “X-EasyITSM-Timestamp.body” with this key.

messengers.intro: A Telegram, MAX, Slack or Microsoft Teams bot accepts tickets from direct messages and sends notifications to people who linked their account in the profile. The server polls Telegram, MAX and Slack or keeps a connection to them, so they need no inbound internet access; Teams sends messages to the server's public address. A reply to a bot message becomes a ticket comment.

tokenHint.max: Issued by the MAX partner platform under Chat bots.
tokenHint.slack: Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) under OAuth & Permissions. Scopes: chat:write, im:history, im:read.
tokenHint.teams: Client secret of the app in Microsoft Entra (Certificates & secrets).

messengers.tokenKeep: Token {{hint}} is saved. Leave the field empty to keep it.
messengers.baseUrlHint: Empty means the official messenger address. A custom address (for example, a proxy) must be in the allowed addresses on the Webhooks tab.
messengers.fields: What to send to the messenger
messengers.fieldsHint: The ticket number is always sent. The messenger's servers store messages, so send only what may leave your perimeter. Confidential tickets never include details.
messengers.confirmDelete: Delete the bot and all links
messengers.appTokenHint: App-Level Token (xapp-…) with connections:write: enable Socket Mode and the message.im event subscription, and allow messages on the App Home tab.
messengers.appTokenKeep: Token {{hint}} is saved. Leave the field empty to keep it.
messengers.appIdHint: From the Azure Bot resource, Configuration section.
messengers.appTenantHint: Tenant ID (Directory ID) or domain, for example contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
messengers.endpointHint: Set this address in the bot settings in Azure and add the Microsoft Teams channel. Unlike other messengers, Microsoft calls this address itself, so it must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.
